Call third-party APIs through the Maton gateway, which injects the credential for an app the user has already connected. Use this skill when the user names a connected app and a concrete action in it - read a mailbox, query a CRM, file an issue, update a spreadsheet, run a query through a connected search or scraping provider. Every call goes to an app the user connected. It is not a general-purpose browser or network client, and it cannot reach a service with no Maton connection. Some connected apps are themselves scraping, browsing, or document-processing services (Firecrawl, Reducto, search providers); using them fetches or processes third-party content on that provider's infrastructure, at the user's explicit request, and is that app's capability rather than this skill's. One kind of step leaves the gateway by design: a few apps (Figma, LinkedIn, Manus, OneDrive, Reducto, SharePoint) move file bytes through a pre-signed URL the app itself returned (uploading to it, checking or cancelling that upload session, or downloading a file or rendered image from it), and that request goes straight to the provider's storage, carrying no Maton credential. It covers installing what it runs on (the `maton` CLI, and the Maton SDK when the user writes code against it), and, for an app that needs one such as iCloud Mail, a Maton bridge: a background service on the user's own computer that starts at login and routes that app's mail connections, installed and removed only with the user's approval. It also administers hosted automation, and that is part of the skill too: creating, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, updating, rolling back, searching, downloading and deleting functions, setting their environment variables, and invoking one at its URL; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including webhook destinations that forward event payloads to an external URL until deleted and rotating a destination's signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying past events, where a replay delivers the event again and re-runs whatever it starts; and watching events locally, including `--exec` handlers that run a script the user supplies on each event. It reads the account's recorded requests, logs and metrics, which include the headers and bodies of past calls; it tags and annotates Maton's record of objects seen in connected apps, which never changes those apps; and it changes account settings such as request and response body capture and context capture, which apply to every connected app and are turned on only when the user asks. Destinations, function deploys and `--exec` handlers are separate, high-risk capabilities beyond a normal API call. Default to read and list calls; every write, connection, function, trigger, destination, replay, or handler needs explicit user confirmation, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID.

skills.summary: Manages free AI models from OpenRouter for OpenClaw. Automatically ranks models by quality, configures fallbacks for rate-limit handling, and updates openclaw.json. Optional Groq, Gemini and Cerebras free tiers are opt-in. Use when the user mentions free AI, OpenRouter, model switching, rate limits, or wants to reduce AI costs.

latestVersion.changelog:
Hardening model selection and auth setup, plus opt-in providers.

- Your own primary model is now left alone. FreeRide only rotates a primary it set itself, and the watcher no longer probes or replaces a primary you configured.
- FreeRide saves your previous primary and fallbacks before changing them. New `freeride restore` (with `--dry-run`) puts them back.
- `freeride auto -f` keeps your primary, marks it as yours, and keeps your own fallback entries.
- API keys are always masked in output, and key-shaped text is scrubbed from error messages. Skill instructions no longer print keys or put them on a command line; keys go in `~/.openclaw/.env`.
- The install command pins the ClawHub CLI version, the skill owner and the skill version. `requests` is capped below 3.
- `--setup-auth` shows exactly what it will add and asks before writing (`--yes` for non-interactive runs). Every file and config key FreeRide writes is now listed in the skill manifest.
- FreeRide refuses to rewrite an `openclaw.json` it cannot parse (JSON5 comments, trailing commas, `$include`), backs the file up to `openclaw.json.freeride-bak` before every change, and writes it atomically.
- Existing per-model settings under `agents.defaults.models` are no longer reset.
- OpenRouter models that charge for output are no longer treated as free.
- Optional providers, off unless you enable them with `--providers`: Groq (tool-capable free models), Gemini (needs `--allow-training-providers`; Google may use free-tier prompts for training), and Cerebras (last, after a live tool-call check). OpenRouter free models stay the default.
- `skill.json` now lists the `rotate` and `restore` commands.
- Added a test suite (`python -m pytest`).
- SKILL.md declares its requirements in the `metadata.openclaw` block ClawHub reads: required and optional env vars (including `FREERIDE_PROVIDERS` and `FREERIDE_ALLOW_TRAINING`), the `openclaw` and Python binaries, and the homepage.
- New `.clawhubignore` keeps the tests out of the published skill.
- License is now MIT-0, matching ClawHub.

For other third party apps, use the api-gateway skill (https://clawhub.ai/byungkyu/api-gateway). Calls run through the `maton` CLI with OAuth login, or over raw HTTP with a Maton API key where the CLI cannot be installed. Every call is authenticated as the user's connection and reaches only what that connection's authorization allows, which the provider enforces on every request; the endpoints documented here are the ones this skill uses, and any other endpoint of this app needs the user to ask for it by name. Default to read and list calls, and confirm every write or new connection with the user. This file also documents the three constructs that turn a Gmail connection into automation, in the order they are used: the connection (the first step), a hosted function that runs a Gmail action through the Maton SDK, and a trigger that calls that function on a schedule or on an event. Running that automation includes administering it, and the skill covers that too: listing, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, searching, updating and deleting functions and their environment variables; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including pointing a destination at a URL the user supplies and rotating its signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying a trigger's past events, where a replay delivers that event again and re-runs whatever it starts; reading the account's request records, logs and metrics to debug a call, which is read-only; querying Maton's context graph, the IDs and relations of Gmail objects the gateway has seen, and adding or removing tags and metadata on those records in Maton; changing account settings, such as turning request and response body capture or context capture on or off; and watching events locally, including running a handler script the user supplies on each event with `--exec`. Every one of these that changes something is a write the user approves individually, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID. Gmail is itself a Maton event source, with its own events in `references/google-mail/triggers.md`; a schedule (`time`) or another connected app's event starts a Gmail function as well, and the files under `references/<source>/triggers.md` describe the sources Maton offers (time, Calendly, GitHub, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Slack, Stripe).

For other third party apps, use the api-gateway skill (https://clawhub.ai/byungkyu/api-gateway). Calls run through the `maton` CLI with OAuth login, or over raw HTTP with a Maton API key where the CLI cannot be installed. Every call is authenticated as the user's connection and reaches only what that connection's authorization allows, which the provider enforces on every request; the endpoints documented here are the ones this skill uses, and any other endpoint of this app needs the user to ask for it by name. Default to read and list calls, and confirm every write or new connection with the user. This file also documents the three constructs that turn a WhatsApp Business connection into automation, in the order they are used: the connection (the first step), a hosted function that runs a WhatsApp Business action through the Maton SDK, and a trigger that calls that function on a schedule or on an event. Running that automation includes administering it, and the skill covers that too: listing, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, searching, updating and deleting functions and their environment variables; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including pointing a destination at a URL the user supplies and rotating its signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying a trigger's past events, where a replay delivers that event again and re-runs whatever it starts; reading the account's request records, logs and metrics to debug a call, which is read-only; changing account settings, such as turning request and response body capture on or off; and watching events locally, including running a handler script the user supplies on each event with `--exec`. Every one of these that changes something is a write the user approves individually, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID. WhatsApp Business itself emits no Maton events: a schedule (`time`) or another connected app's event starts a WhatsApp Business function, and the files under `references/<source>/triggers.md` describe the sources Maton offers (time, Calendly, GitHub, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Slack, Stripe).

# Changelog - n8n Enhanced Workflow Management Skill

## Version 2.0.0 - 10 Feb  2026

### 🎉 Major Enhancement Release

Complete redesign of the n8n skill with comprehensive workflow lifecycle management capabilities.

### ✨ New Features

#### Testing & Validation
- **Structure Validation:** `n8n_tester.py` validates workflow integrity
  - Node and connection validation
  - Credential checking
  - Configuration verification
  - Flow analysis
- **Dry-Run Testing:** Test workflows with sample data before activation
- **Test Suites:** Run multiple test cases against workflows
- **Validation Reports:** Human-readable test reports with errors and warnings

#### Execution Monitoring
- **Enhanced Execution Tracking:** Real-time execution monitoring
- **Detailed Statistics:** Success/failure rates, execution patterns
- **Error Analysis:** Identify and categorize failure patterns
- **Retry Logic:** Built-in retry support for failed executions

#### Performance Optimization
- **Performance Analysis:** `n8n_optimizer.py` provides comprehensive metrics
  - Execution metrics (success rate, failure patterns)
  - Node analysis (complexity, expensive operations)
  - Connection analysis (parallel paths, bottlenecks)
  - Performance scoring (0-100)
- **Bottleneck Detection:** Identify workflow performance issues
  - Sequential expensive operations
  - High failure rates
  - Missing error handling
- **Optimization Suggestions:** Actionable recommendations
  - Parallel execution opportunities
  - Caching strategies
  - Batch processing
  - Error handling improvements
  - Complexity reduction
- **Optimization Reports:** Human-readable performance reports

### 📝 API Extensions

#### n8n_api.py Enhancements
- `validate_workflow()` - Validate workflow structure
- `dry_run_workflow()` - Test workflow with mock data
- `get_workflow_statistics()` - Get execution statistics
- `analyze_workflow_performance()` - Performance analysis
- CLI support for `create`, `validate`, and `stats` commands

#### New Modules
- **n8n_tester.py** - Testing and validation
  - Structure validation
  - Dry-run execution
  - Test suite runner
  - Report generation
- **n8n_optimizer.py** - Performance optimization
  - Performance analysis
  - Bottleneck detection
  - Optimization suggestions
  - Report generation

### 📚 Documentation

#### New Documentation
- **README.md** - Quick start guide with examples
- **SKILL.md** - Comprehensive documentation (16KB)
  - All CLI commands
  - Python API examples
  - Common workflows
  - Best practices
  - Troubleshooting guide
- **templates/README.md** - Template documentation
  - Template descriptions
  - Configuration guides
  - Test data examples
- **CHANGELOG.md** - This file

#### Updated Documentation
- Enhanced quick reference
- Added validation examples
- Performance optimization guides
- Template usage examples

### 🗂️ File Structure

```
~/clawd/skills/n8n/
├── README.md                   # Quick start guide
├── SKILL.md                    # Comprehensive documentation
├── CHANGELOG.md                # This file
├── scripts/
│   ├── n8n_api.py             # Core API client (extended)
│   ├── n8n_tester.py          # NEW: Testing & validation
│   └── n8n_optimizer.py       # NEW: Performance optimization
└── references/
    └── api.md
```

### 🔧 Technical Improvements

- **Modular Design:** Separated concerns into specialized modules
- **Error Handling:** Comprehensive error checking and reporting
- **Import Flexibility:** Support for both direct and module imports
- **Validation Logic:** Standalone validation without API dependency
- **Performance Metrics:** Multi-dimensional workflow analysis
- **Extensible Templates:** Easy to add new workflow templates

### 📊 Metrics & Analysis

New performance metrics tracked:
- Execution success/failure rates
- Node complexity scores (0-100)
- Performance scores (0-100)
- Health status (excellent/good/fair/poor)
- Bottleneck severity levels
- Optimization priorities (high/medium/low)

### 🎯 Use Cases

The enhanced skill now supports:
1. **Rapid Prototyping:** Deploy templates and test within minutes
2. **Quality Assurance:** Validate and test before production deployment
3. **Performance Tuning:** Identify and resolve bottlenecks
4. **Continuous Monitoring:** Track workflow health over time
5. **Best Practices:** Built-in optimization recommendations

### 🔄 Migration from v1.0

No breaking changes. All v1.0 functionality preserved and enhanced:
- `list-workflows` - Still works
- `get-workflow` - Still works
- `activate` / `deactivate` - Still works
- `list-executions` / `get-execution` - Still works
- `execute` - Still works

New commands added:
- `create` - Create workflows from templates or files
- `validate` - Validate workflow structure
- `stats` - Get execution statistics

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed import issues in testing module
- Added standalone validation for file-based workflows
- Improved error messages for missing credentials
- Enhanced connection validation logic

### ⚡ Performance

- Validation runs without API calls for file-based workflows
- Efficient execution monitoring with configurable polling
- Optimized statistics calculation for large execution histories

### 🔐 Security

- No credentials stored in templates (placeholders only)
- Environment variable-based authentication
- Validation runs safely without modifying workflows

### 📦 Dependencies

No new dependencies
- `requests` (existing)
- `json`, `sys`, `argparse`, `pathlib`, `typing` (standard library)

### 🚀 Future Roadmap

Planned for future releases:
- Additional workflow templates (10+ total)
- Workflow versioning and rollback
- A/B testing framework
- Cost tracking and optimization
- Workflow dependencies and orchestration
- Visual workflow builder web UI
- AI-powered workflow optimization
- Integration testing framework

### 👥 Contributors

- Enhanced n8n skill for Clawdbot/Thomas
- Based on requirements for SaaS automation workflows

### 📄 License

Part of the Clawdbot skills library.

skills.summary: Salesforce CRM API integration with managed OAuth. Install only if you need Salesforce CRM administration. Connect with the narrowest Salesforce permissions available, prefer sandbox orgs for destructive or batch work, verify the intended connection ID before each request, and revoke unused connections promptly. This integration can mutate CRM records — approve only specific write actions after checking the exact sObject, record IDs, and consequence. For other third party apps, use the api-gateway skill (https://clawhub.ai/byungkyu/api-gateway). Calls run through the `maton` CLI with OAuth login, or over raw HTTP with a Maton API key where the CLI cannot be installed. Every call is authenticated as the user's connection and reaches only what that connection's authorization allows, which the provider enforces on every request; the endpoints documented here are the ones this skill uses, and any other endpoint of this app needs the user to ask for it by name. Default to read and list calls, and confirm every write or new connection with the user. This file also documents the three constructs that turn a Salesforce connection into automation, in the order they are used: the connection (the first step), a hosted function that runs a Salesforce action through the Maton SDK, and a trigger that calls that function on a schedule or on an event. Running that automation includes administering it, and the skill covers that too: listing, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, searching, updating and deleting functions and their environment variables; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including pointing a destination at a URL the user supplies and rotating its signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying a trigger's past events, where a replay delivers that event again and re-runs whatever it starts; reading the account's request records, logs and metrics to debug a call, which is read-only; changing account settings, such as turning request and response body capture on or off; and watching events locally, including running a handler script the user supplies on each event with `--exec`. Every one of these that changes something is a write the user approves individually, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID. Salesforce itself emits no Maton events: a schedule (`time`) or another connected app's event starts a Salesforce function, and the files under `references/<source>/triggers.md` describe the sources Maton offers (time, Calendly, GitHub, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Slack, Stripe).

skills.summary: Read and convert documents with the SwiftText CLI. Use it instead of opening Pages, Numbers, Keynote or Word, or scripting them with AppleScript.

latestVersion.changelog:
**Digitised books render as printed. `render --footnote-labels source` keeps the footnote numbers written in the Markdown (`[^31]` shows 31), `--footnotes page` now fills every page with a custom `@page` size or wide side margins, and `ocr -m` no longer reports scan shadows and show-through as images. `docx -m` writes Word tables as Markdown tables.**

### Render
- **`--footnote-labels source`** (#270). A footnote whose id is a number, or ends in one after a separator (`[^31]`, `[^k2-48]`), is labelled with that number instead of the running count. Other ids keep the running count; the default is unchanged.
- **`--footnotes page` respects `@page` size and side margins** (#269). A custom trim size (for example 170 × 240 mm) or wide margins no longer leave every other page nearly empty.
- HTML renderer: inline-blocks are laid out, corners are rounded and bold is synthesised where a face is missing (#266).

### OCR
- **`ocr -m`: no phantom `![Image]()` blocks** over scan-edge shadows and grey show-through on scanned pages; real photos are kept (#268).

### DOCX
- **`docx -m` emits GFM pipe tables from native Word tables** instead of bold paragraphs (#258).
- Rendering to DOCX: links inside footnotes are clickable (#260); quotes and further paragraphs inside list items are kept (#261).

### Project
- Releases update the Homebrew tap (#256) and publish the SwiftText agent skill to ClawHub (#257).
- CI: Windows zlib import lib name (#263); Android emulator cold boot and 25-minute cap (#265).

@shopify/shop 1.3.0

## Ask a store directly

Use `shop ask` to ask a store about its products, policies, or other resources. Ground questions in the store's resource IDs and continue a returned conversation for follow-ups. Add `--format md` for readable answers and links.

Use `shop order get <id>` with an ID returned by order search to read one Shop-tracked order or package without searching your history again.

The advanced search schema now exposes `catalog.filters.media` through `--arguments`, with image, video, external-video, and 3D-model media types.

- Similarity searches now reject requests with more than one `like` entry before sending. The input remains an array.
- Use your host's native plugin installation; the portable plugin entrypoint has been removed.
- Rerun `shop skill --install` after upgrading to refresh installed skills and their bundled copies of Shop.

skills.summary: GitHub API integration with managed OAuth. Access repositories, issues, pull requests, commits, branches, and users. Use this skill when users want to interact with GitHub repositories, manage issues and PRs, search code, or automate workflows. For other third party apps, use the api-gateway skill (https://clawhub.ai/byungkyu/api-gateway). Calls run through the `maton` CLI with OAuth login, or over raw HTTP with a Maton API key where the CLI cannot be installed. Every call is authenticated as the user's connection and reaches only what that connection's authorization allows, which the provider enforces on every request; the endpoints documented here are the ones this skill uses, and any other endpoint of this app needs the user to ask for it by name. Default to read and list calls, and confirm every write or new connection with the user. This file also documents the three constructs that turn a GitHub connection into automation, in the order they are used: the connection (the first step), a hosted function that runs a GitHub action through the Maton SDK, and a trigger that calls that function on a schedule or on an event. Running that automation includes administering it, and the skill covers that too: listing, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, searching, updating and deleting functions and their environment variables; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including pointing a destination at a URL the user supplies and rotating its signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying a trigger's past events, where a replay delivers that event again and re-runs whatever it starts; reading the account's request records, logs and metrics to debug a call, which is read-only; querying Maton's context graph, the IDs and relations of GitHub objects the gateway has seen, and adding or removing tags and metadata on those records in Maton; changing account settings, such as turning request and response body capture or context capture on or off; and watching events locally, including running a handler script the user supplies on each event with `--exec`. Every one of these that changes something is a write the user approves individually, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID. GitHub is itself a Maton event source, with its own events in `references/github/triggers.md`; a schedule (`time`) or another connected app's event starts a GitHub function as well, and the files under `references/<source>/triggers.md` describe the sources Maton offers (time, Calendly, GitHub, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Slack, Stripe).

latestVersion.changelog:
Complete rewrite of the execution model and update to Notion API 2025-09-03.

Breaking
- Removed the notion-cli dependency. All operations are now plain curl calls
  against the official API. The previous version documented a CLI that was
  never distributed, so its commands could not run as written.

Changed
- Pinned to Notion-Version 2025-09-03. Databases are now addressed as data
  sources; added guidance on the database_id vs data_source_id split, which is
  the most common source of 404s after the upgrade.
- Token format updated to ntn_ (secret_ still supported).
- Profiles now have a concrete mechanism: ~/.config/notion/<profile>.key, with
  an explicit NOTION_API_KEY taking precedence over NOTION_PROFILE.
- Safety rules moved to the top of the skill as five operating rules applied
  before any request.
- Schema-change flow tightened: fetch current schema, diff, present to the
  user, apply only what was confirmed. Additive changes preferred over
  in-place property retyping, which discards incompatible values.

Added
- Pagination handling (has_more / next_cursor) with a rule against summarizing
  a database from a single unpaginated response.
- Error reference table covering validation_error, restricted_resource,
  object_not_found, conflict_error, and rate_limited, with what each usually
  means in practice.
- Notes that GET /pages/{id} does not return body content, that nested blocks
  require separate calls, that formula and rollup properties are read-only,
  and that view filters are UI-only.
- Property format reference including status, people, and phone_number.
